history.dynasty: Mushika (Kolathiri) dynasty; consecration legend attributed to Parashurama
history.period: Legends date it to Treta Yuga; rebuilt into present form in the early 11th century (verify)
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 1727 / Rajarajeshwara Temple — 'Taliparamba Shakti Peetha' is not a separate shrine: the Taliparamba Rajarajeswara Temple itself is identified as one of the Shakti Peethas. Legend says the head of Goddess Sati fell here after Shiva's tandava following Sati's self-immolation at the Daksha yagna, and the site is counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala consecrated by Parashurama. The swayambhu Shiva lingam (~3 ft, gold-covered) is linked to kings Mandhata, Muchukunda and Satasoma and to sages Agastya and Parashurama; Sri Rama is believed to have worshipped here on his return from Lanka. Unique customs: no kodimaram (flagstaff), tulsi (not bilva) offered to the lingam, women permitted only after the Athazha Pooja (~7:15-8:30 PM), and no pradosha celebrations. Administered by the Malabar Devaswom Board.

name: Taliparamba Shakti Peetha
town_description: Taliparamba (Thaliparamba) is a town in Kannur district, North Kerala, about 25 km north of Kannur city, in the ancient region of Perinchellur (Perumchelloor). It is a major religious centre of North Malabar, forming a trinity of revered temples with the Vaidyanatha temple at Kanhirangat and the Krishna temple at Trichambaram. Well connected by road and rail (Pazhayangadi station ~15 km), with Kannur International Airport the nearest airport.

travel.road: Frequent buses from Kannur to Taliparamba; autos from Taliparamba bus stand to the temple
